_README: IDENTITY REGISTRY for the terminal resolver (scripts/mt5_terminals.py).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The resolver used to pick the install whose journal was
written most recently. That is wrong in a specific, measured way: on
2026-09-19 the DEAD Deriv install (49E0383C) had a logs/20260919.log written
at 15:58 reading 'MetaTrader 5 Terminal x64 build 6182 started for Deriv.com
Limited'. A terminal that merely BOOTED satisfied every recency test, so an
install with no account, no EA and no relation to the live venue was a
plausible answer to 'which terminal are we trading on?'.
The fix is to identify installs by the ACCOUNT NUMBER in their journals
rather than by mtime. MT5 writes unambiguous identity lines:
'1428765': authorized on Upcomers-Server
'1428765': terminal synchronized with Upcomers Ltd.: 0 positions, ...
So an install that cites an account we do not trade can NEVER be selected,
however recently it was touched.
EXCLUSION COMES FROM 'active' ALONE. Any install citing an account that is
not the active one is classified foreign and excluded from every fallback,
whether or not it appears in the 'retired' list below. The retired list does
not do the excluding -- it gives the excluded install a NAME, so a refusal
can say 'that is the closed MIDASTOUCH gold install' rather than only
'acct 140778269'. Keep the entries current for that reason, not for safety:
the safety is in 'active' being correct.
Update 'active' whenever the trading account changes. If the declared account
is not found in any install, the resolver says so rather than falling back to
recency. An install citing NO account is eligible but flagged as unconfirmed,
so ambiguity is reported instead of hidden.
Override for CI/tests: MITEMSHUB_MT5_ACCOUNT=<number> replaces the declared
active account; MITEMSHUB_MT5_REGISTRY=<path> points at a different registry.

active.note: Funded evaluation account. The only install that may be resolved as live.
account_size_note: THE SIZING BASIS FOR EVERY ENGINE, IN ONE PLACE.
It was in three places before this field existed, all disagreeing: the parity
harness ran the EA in a tester funded at $1,000, pinned the EA's paper-sizing
input at $5,000 to match the python research engine's own START_EQUITY, and the
EA's prop governor defaulted to sizing off whatever balance the tester gave it.
A trade set produced under a $1,000 basis is not evidence about this account,
and nothing said so out loud.
Readers must REFUSE rather than default when this is absent (see
mt5_terminals.active_account_size): a missing basis is an unanswerable question,
Update it whenever the evaluation size changes, in the same commit as the

retired.reason: Program closed and the account defunded; the Deriv terminal was uninstalled. Its data directories remain on disk and must never be resolved as live. See docs/MIDASTOUCH_CLOSEOUT_20260919.md and docs/GOLD_SURFACE_RETIREMENT_20260919.md.
